key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produces denser, harder Cr3C2–NiCr coatings than conventional APS, but this mainly improves wear resistance rather than high-angle erosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: For wear-prone components, switching to axial-feed HV-APS can improve coating performance without changing the coating chemistry, making it a practical route to extend service life.
method: Compared conventional APS (radial powder injection, A60 torch) with HV-APS (axial powder feeding, Axial III torch).
Deposited Cr3C2–NiCr cermet coatings on S235 steel and analyzed microstructure, phase composition, hardness, porosity, erosion, and tribology.
Evaluated performance using erosion testing at 90° impact and ball-on-disc wear testing under 30 N load.
evidence_signal: HV-APS reduced porosity from 11.99% to 6.16% and increased microhardness from 897 HV0.2 to 1141 HV0.2, while lowering wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm3; erosion rates remained nearly unchanged (0.20 vs 0.19 mg/g).
watch_item: The HV-APS advantage did not translate into better erosion resistance at 90° impact, so process selection should be based on the dominant service wear mode.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
